about: How `name < … > (` reads: the types of a template's call, or comparisons when name holds a value where it is written (spec/reference.md, 3.4). A case is a whole `text`; `formatted` is how it prints back, `error` the line:col of the error that refuses it. Read by python/tests/test_conformance.py and rust/tests/conformance.rs.

cases.name: comparisons_in_arguments
cases.about: Two comparisons side by side, of the graph's inputs: no call of a

cases.name: comparisons_chained
cases.about: a < b > (c) is two comparisons, which are refused, not a call of a

cases.name: bound_name
cases.about: A name an earlier statement bound

cases.name: bound_in_a_frame
cases.about: A frame is no scope: its names hold after it

cases.name: not_yet_bound
cases.about: A name bound later is no value before its statement: the types of a call

cases.name: body_item
cases.about: An item of a call with a body, inside that body

cases.name: body_item_alias
cases.about: An item keyed with as, inside its body

cases.name: body_item_stays_inside
cases.about: After the body, its item is no value

cases.name: nameless_graph_input
cases.about: An input of a graph with no name, which sees the names around too

cases.name: template_call
template_passes_its_type
cases.about: Inside a template, a call that passes its type on

cases.name: unknown_name
cases.about: A name that is no value: read as a call with types, the reader's checker refuses it
